newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says UK bank supervision changes a mistake.
newsitem.headline: IBCA says UK bank supervision changes a mistake.

text.p: European credit rating agency IBCA said the UK government's plans to merge banking supervision and securities regulation was a mistake and had not been undertaken in this shape in any other major banking centre.

In reaction to UK Chancellor Gordon Brown's announcement on Tuesday, Robin Monro-Davies, the managing director of IBCA, said the Bank of England would have to remain the lender of last resort and therefore retain a substantial staff.
"The result will be unnecessary duplication of effort," said Monro-Davies in a statement.
Separating the two functions would not neccessarily result in greater efficiency, he added.
In a statement to Parliament on Tuesday, Brown said the government would immediately start working on the legislation to reform the regulatory system.
Supervision for Britain's banking sector would be transfered from the Bank of England to the Securities and Investments Board (SIB), which would become the single regulator, underpinned by statute.
Monro-Davies said he was concerned about the sheer power and size of the newly expanded SIB, which risked becoming "a huge and unresponsive bureaucracy".
